subject: Post-demo: procurement path & PO vs card follow-ups
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@skybridge.energy>, Rachel Zhu <rachel@skybridge.energy>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: procurement path & PO vs card follow-ups

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the time. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed on the call: 

- Current ask: confirm commercial onboarding route (PO via AP vs corporate card) and any marketplace procurement requirement.
- Your constraints mentioned: AP requires vendor setup + 30+ day lead time for new vendors; corporate card has single-card limit of $25k/month.
- Marketplace option (AWS/GCP marketplace) was of interest as it can simplify billing but needs procurement sign-off.

Attached: Redwood_Procurement_FAQ.pdf — short FAQ on PO process, vendor setup requirements, and marketplace notes. Also added a sample MAAP (vendor data) spreadsheet for your procurement team (Skybridge_MAAP_Request.xlsx).

Next steps:
1) Tom to confirm whether AP will accept marketplace invoices (billing to Skybridge vendor ID) or require Redwood to be set up as a vendor.
2) If going PO, share preferred PO template and onboarding contact; we can expedite vendor packet.
3) If card is the route, confirm monthly spend profile and whether we should set up net-30 invoicing for initial committed spend.

Happy to jump on a 15-min follow-up with procurement if that helps.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0117

Attachment: Redwood_Procurement_FAQ.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
Attachment: Skybridge_MAAP_Request.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@skybridge.energy>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Zhu <rachel@skybridge.energy>
Date: 2027-08-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement path & PO vs card follow-ups

Thanks Jonas — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from procurement side: 

- Marketplace: our AP team prefers marketplace billing when available because it avoids vendor onboarding. Do you publish on AWS Marketplace or GCP Marketplace for hosted billing? If yes, procurement will likely push for that.
- Vendor setup: if marketplace is not an option, we'll need a vendor packet; our process requires W9, COI, bank details and a signed vendor agreement. Lead time is typically 3-5 weeks.
- PO vs Card: we can do a card for initial POC spend under $25k, but recurring production spend will require PO and preferred net-30 terms. Is Redwood able to provide net-30 invoicing once vendor onboarding is complete?

Also attaching our PO template if that helps (will send separately via procurement).

Tom Ellis
Head of Procurement | Skybridge Energy
t.ellis@skybridge.energy

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@skybridge.energy>, Rachel Zhu <rachel@skybridge.energy>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement path & PO vs card follow-ups

Appreciate the clarifications, Tom. Short answers below — copying Ben from our finance team to confirm operational details: 

- Marketplace: Redwood currently supports AWS Marketplace billing for our hosted API tiers and has a listing for the standard inference plan. We are in process of enabling GCP Marketplace for a subset of enterprise customers but that is not generally available yet. If Skybridge prefers Marketplace, AWS Marketplace invoicing is an option today.
- Net-30 invoicing: yes, we support net-30 for customers after vendor setup and execution of our master services agreement (MSA). For bigger commitments we typically add a simple SOW for initial term.
- Vendor packet: attached FAQ includes the standard list; Ben can follow up with the exact COI/W9/bank detail email and expedite the vendor form if needed.

Action: Ben — can you confirm whether Redwood needs a signed MSA before taking a PO, or if we can accept a PO against our standard terms and attach the MSA concurrently? Also estimate onboarding lead time if procurement sends vendor packet today.

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachment: Redwood_Procurement_FAQ.pdf (PDF)

> On Mon, Aug 14, 2027 at 11:03 AM Tom Ellis <t.ellis@skybridge.energy> wrote:
> > Thanks Jonas — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from procurement side: ...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@skybridge.energy>
Cc: Rachel Zhu <rachel@skybridge.energy>
Date: 2027-08-14T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement path & PO vs card follow-ups

Hi Tom / Jonas — Ben from Finance here. Quick operational notes and what we need to move forward: 

- MSA vs PO: We can accept a PO against our standard commercial terms if the PO references the MSA template. In practice, procurement can issue a PO and we’ll countersign the MSA within our standard SLA for legal review. If procurement needs an executed MSA before PO, that may add 1-2 weeks depending on redlines.
- Required docs: W9, COI (if requested), bank account details (for ACH), and a completed vendor setup form. I can email a single consolidated packet to your procurement alias.
- Lead time: once we receive a complete packet, vendor setup typically completes in 7-10 business days; expedited requests (where procurement confirms priority) can shorten to 3-5 business days.
- Marketplace note: if you invoice via AWS Marketplace, vendor setup is not required on our side but Marketplace fees apply and billing will be through AWS.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Tom — share whether procurement prefers AWS Marketplace or direct vendor onboarding.
2) If direct onboarding: please send PO template + procurement contact and I’ll send the consolidated packet and a one‑page checklist to speed things up.
3) If Marketplace: confirm the AWS customer ID and we’ll pull together the marketplace listing link and pricing notes.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call with procurement to walk through the packet if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0199

Attachment: Redwood_Vendor_Packet_Checklist.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
